top.title: Hurricanes 5, Islanders 3
top.description: ELMONT, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 05: Brandon Bussi #32 of the Carolina Hurricanes saves a shot from Anthony Duclair #11 of the New York Islanders during the first period at UBS Arena on November 05, 2026 in Elmont, New York. (Photo by Steven Ryan/NHLI via Getty Images) | NHLI via Getty Images According to coach Rod Brind’Amour the team was “not at its best”, but the Carolina Hurricanes scored twice in the third period and held on to defeat the New York Islanders, 5-3 on Thursday night at UBS Arena. The Canes improved their record to 13-3-2 on the season. Brandon Bussi made 24 saves on the 27 shots he faced to pick up his third win of the season. Logan Stankoven got things started just 57 seconds into the game when he took a pass from Jackson Blake and ripped it past goalie Semyon Varlamov. Stankoven now has a team leading 11 goals for the season. Blake added to his team-high assist total to 14. A couple of minutes later, Jesperi Kotkaniemi tipped in a Jordan Martinook pass to make it 2-0 and it looked like Carolina was flying. But they took their feet off the gas and the Islanders got back in the game. The home team tied the score at two but the Canes would strike again on an Andrei Svechnokov goal in the second. The Islanders tied it at three before the end of the period and even though the Canes were outshooting NY, they seemed to be reeling a bit. But they came out strong in the third period. Will Carrier knocked in the game-winner off a Svechnikov shot 15 minutes and change into the third and that would be enough to finish off the Islanders. Jalen Chatfield fought for a loose puck and put in a long shot into an empty net to complete the scoring. All in all, it was the team’s best effort but they did what they needed to do to get the win. Next up will be a game at home on Saturday night against the Blackhawks which will be their last game before the trip to Finland. Notes: Kotkaniemi had a team low 8 minutes of ice time. He now has 5 goals and 3 assists and has played well recently. Not sure what else he needs to do to see more ice time. He also had 2 hits and was 50% in the faceoff circle. Taylor Hall returned to action and played just over 10 minutes. The Canes went 34% in the circle. The Hurricanes ended up outshooting the home team, 39-27. top.title: Jaguars move up in AFC standings after squashing Ravens
top.description: (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars won on Thursday night and moved up in the AFC standings. With the Pittsburgh Steelers on a bye, the Jags’ position will be at least third by the end of the weekend, and they can move into second and a tie for first place if everything goes their way. Let’s not get too far ahead of ourselves. Here are the standings as we stand now, then we will get into the rest of the weekend. AFC playoff standings after the Jaguars win 1. Buffalo Bills (6-1) 2. Denver Broncos (6-2, 3-1 AFC) 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2, 5-2) 4. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2, 3-2 AFC) 5. Kansas City Chiefs (5-2, 5-1 AFC) 6. Cincinnati Bengals (5-2, 4-2 AFC) 7. New England Patriots (5-3, 5-1 AFC) 8. Cleveland Browns (5-3, 3-3 AFC) 9. Las Vegas Raiders (4-4) 10. Baltimore Ravens (4-5) 11. Houston Texans (2-5) 12. New York Jets (2-6, 2-3 AFC) 13. Indianapolis Colts (2-6, 1-5 AFC) 14. Miami Dolphins (1-6) 15. Tennessee Titans (1-7) 16. Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) Explaining the 6-2 tiebreaker between the Jaguars, Steelers, and Broncos The Jaguars, Broncos, and Steelers all go in together and while they will all play each other eventually, that hasn’t happened so we skip the head-to-head-to-head tiebreaker. The tiebreaker moves to conference record where the 3-1 Broncos best the 5-2 Jaguars and the 3-2 Steelers. Denver is the two seed. The Broncos and Steelers haven’t played each other yet, so the AFC record is applied again here and the 5-2 Jaguars slip ahead of the 3-2 Steelers. Jacksonville is the three seed and Pittsburgh is the four seed. How high in the standings can the Jaguars get before the end of Week 8? The Steelers are on a bye, but the Jaguars are already ahead of them. The Broncos can lose to the Carolina Panthers and fall to 6-3. The Buffalo Bills, though, can’t fall behind Jacksonville. The Bills could lose to the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night to fall into that 6-2 tie, but they are 5-1 in the AFC and that isn’t going to change. The highest the Jaguars can get is second behind Buffalo — for now.

top.title: UNC vs. Wofford game preview, info, prediction and more
top.description: The North Carolina Tar Heels return to action on Friday night, looking to go 2-0 on the young college basketball season. But in order to do that, they are going to need to play better than they did in their season-opening win over Western Carolina. While UNC got a win, they had to hold off a Catamounts team that pushed them to the end. UNC played poorly on both sides of the court and, honestly, are a little lucky they were able to win the game. But a win is a win and North Carolina is moving forward and focusing on the second game in the Michael Malone era. Next up? The Wofford Terriers. The Tar Heels' schedule gets tougher moving forward, so racking up some wins here early on will be key. It could also help them earn some more confidence as well before that schedule picks up. While there were struggles in the first game, this is another opportunity. It's one in which they can use to figure some things out in terms of rotations and defensive sets. This will give Malone a chance to see some things with his roster on the court as well. Key to Victory Rebounding. The Tar Heels were outrebounded by the Catamounts 41-32 on Monday night and it almost cost them the game. It's unusual to see this program get outrebounded by an inferior opponent, even with it being the season-opener. North Carolina's roster doesn't have a dominant big man just yet and they are going to rely on Sayon Keita to be that guy. With Cameron Fenns ineligible, the depth takes a hit. The Tar Heels cant afford to keep being bad at rebounding because it's going to cost them if they do. Something to Watch Point guard role. In the season opener, we saw Neo Avdalas be the primary ball-handler on offense. But it didn't work out so well. The lack of a true point guard really hurt them in the opener. Will Malone make an adjustment? And if so, then who? This team may not have a true point guard option ready to go at the moment which could hurt them. top.title: Fort Defiance volleyball cruises to regional final
top.description: After more than a week off, Fort Defiance showed no signs of rust in its playoff opener Nov. 5. The top seed in Region 2B rolled over No. 4 Clarke County 25-11, 25-10, 25-20 in the Region 2B semifinals. With the win, Fort Defiance will host No. 2 Madison County for the regional championship Nov. 10. Both teams have already earned a spot in the Class 2 state playoffs. Fort Defiance was on fire from the start. They didn't have a single serving or hitting error in the opening set, setting the tone for the night. The 75-minute match was short work for Fort, which is aiming to reach the state championship game for the third season in a row. Junior Caroline Hanger couldn't remember playing a set with no errors. "It was just great. Everything was just flowing," said Hanger, who finished with 10 kills. "All the hitters were doing so good and the defense was picking everything up." Freshman Maddie Gale had another all-around good game, finishing with six kills, 18 assists and four aces. Senior libero Norah Anderson had nine digs and four aces, while junior middle Harper Carter had six kills and sophomore Abbi Bright had seven digs and Alexis Miller added six assists in the win. "I think if we keep playing like how we played tonight, I feel confidence in our skills," said Hanger. Coach Amber Pitsenbarger did a lot of skill work with her players throughout the week without any games because of a first-round playoff bye, but maybe the biggest factor in keeping Fort sharp was how the coaching staff approached last Thursday and this past Tuesday, which would have typically been game days. "We went through the game-day routine," Pitsenbarger said. "We did our serve-around routine and we actually just played." The coach said they had a match between starters and non-starters and some other scrimmages just to stay sharp. It helped. Hanger liked having the week off, saying the team probably needed it after a long regular season, but she liked staying in the game-day routine even without an actual game that counted. Next up is Madison, which advanced to play Fort with a four-set win over No. 6 Stuarts Draft. Madison won 25-19, 25-17, 16-25, 25-19. Addyson Dameron had 25 assists and nine digs to lead Draft, while Lily May added 16 kills and Kylie Morland had 15 kills and 10 digs in the loss. Addy Coyner and Serenity Hamric both finished with 10 digs. Madison enters the match unbeaten at 23-0, but they did lose to Fort Defiance in a scrimmage in mid-August. "We played them in a scrimmage but it was very, very early," Pitsenbarger said. "We know they're going to be good. We've ended their season several times so we know they're going to be coming for us. I expect it to be a really good matchup." top.title: Kozo Tashima: Japan leader looking to bring 'integrity' to FIFA
top.description: Kozo Tashima has announced he intends to run for the FIFA presidency (Toshifumi KITAMURA) Kozo Tashima first started playing football after watching the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, and since then he has dedicated his life to developing the sport's growth in Japan. The 68-year-old is set to become the first person from Japan to run for the FIFA presidency after announcing he would stand against Gianni Infantino in football's governing body's election in March. Tashima has served as a football player, coach and bureaucrat and has a reputation for being a safe pair of hands. He rarely makes headlines, and one of the few times he appeared outside the sport pages was when he became one of the first public figures in Japan to contract coronavirus in March 2020. He spent time studying at the German Sport University Cologne and said the experience changed the way he saw sport's purpose in society. He says his decision to run for the FIFA presidency was based on a belief that "in this age of business and money, sport must firmly uphold its integrity". "The worst thing would be if he (Infantino) were to continue without an election," he told reporters after announcing his candidacy. "I feel this is a test of whether FIFA has the ability to cleanse itself." Tashima was born in southern Kumamoto and captained his team to the title in Japan's prestigious national high school championship. With no professional football in the country at the time, he had ambitions of becoming a PE teacher and enrolled at a university, where he was called up to play for Japan's full national team. He joined a club in Japan's amateur league after graduating but soon retired as a player and went to Germany to study to become a coach. He described his "profound shock" at the players' superior skills and the way football was viewed there. "Even back in 1980, the training in Germany was hugely scientific and systematic," he said. "Everything seemed like a different world from Japan, and it was a big culture shock for me." - Experienced hand - Tashima returned home determined to use what he had learned in Germany and help develop Japanese football. He coached a university team before joining the Japan Football Association (JFA), where he worked on development programmes and coached the country's national teams at various youth levels. He rose through the JFA ranks and was elected president in 2016, while also serving on the Asian Football Confederation executive committee and the FIFA Council. His reign as JFA chief saw him fire Japan coach Vahid Halilhodzic two months before the 2018 World Cup in Russia. Halilhodzic, who was unpopular with the players, was replaced by Akira Nishino, and Japan reached the last 16, where they were eliminated by Belgium. "Some people told me that I wasn't the one who hired Halilhodzic so it wouldn't be my fault if the team lost," Tashima said. "But as president, all the responsibility lay with me." top.description: Sep 19, 2026; College Station, Texas, USA; The SEC logo seen on a down chain during the game between the Texas A&M Aggies and the Kentucky Wildcats at Kyle Field. Mandatory Credit: Maria Lysaker-Imagn Images The College Football Playoff selection committee caused quite a stir this week when it ranked two-loss Alabama No. 5 in its first rankings of the season. The decision left plenty of fans and analysts convinced that the SEC is getting the benefit of the doubt from the committee once again. Now, Danny Kanell is predicting things are going to get even worse. The former Florida State quarterback warned that there will be a push for an 8-4 SEC team to make the playoff this season. Alabama’s Controversial Ranking Alabama has losses to Georgia and Tennessee this season, including a 26-10 defeat in Knoxville on Oct. 17. Even so, the committee ranked the Crimson Tide at No. 5, making them one of the highest-ranked two-loss teams in College Football Playoff history. To make matters worse for critics, Tennessee came in all the way down at No. 13, outside of the playoff field. Texas, which beat Tennessee in that same stadium back in September, was ranked two spots behind Alabama at No. 7. The debate also comes as the playoff is set to grow even bigger. Last month, the CFP was reportedly nearing a deal to expand to 24 teams beginning in 2027, which Kanell supported. “I think this could be a great day for college football. I’m actually excited,” Kanell said at the time, on CBS Sports . ‘Brace Yourselves’ Needless to say, the decision to rank Alabama all the way at No. 5 received a lot of pushback. While a lot of the criticism was directed at Alabama specifically, Kanell took aim at the SEC as a whole, predicting an even bigger push for the conference this postseason. “I hope everyone is prepared for the push for an 8-4 SEC team in the college football playoff. THIS year. Brace yourselves. It’s coming. They have no shame,” Kanell wrote on X . Not everyone agreed with Kanell’s logic, though. Several pointed out that his support for a 24-team playoff would open the door for teams with even more losses. “As opposed to your 24-team CFP where they’ll push for a 7-5 SEC team – great work!” wrote Josh Pate , college football analyst for ESPN, On3, and Yahoo Sports. “you meant 5-7…7 good SEC losses – huge resume builders,” Kanell replied . “But with the 24 team CFP that’s gonna be pretty much automatic. Choose your fighter brother,” wrote Jake Crain , host of On3’s Crain & Cone . Former Georgia star David Pollack, host of See Ball Get Ball , decided to have some fun with it. “It Just Means More! Going to be sweet @CFBPlayoff #bestconference #toptobottom,” Pollack wrote . The controversy isn’t going to stop anytime soon. But maybe next year, the 24-team playoff could help the debate a little bit with more teams included in the field. top.title: ‘Not even close’- Draymond Green fires back at Kendrick Perkins after brutal ‘liability’ claim
top.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Draymond Green has fired back at Kendrick Perkins after the ESPN analyst labelled the Golden State Warriors forward a liability rather than an asset following his latest ejection. Green acknowledged that he is no longer the player he once was, but insisted his basketball intelligence still separates him from his former NBA rival. The exchange followed Golden State’s 116-113 victory over the Phoenix Suns, during which Green was ejected after a heated altercation involving Suns centre Khaman Maluach and Dillon Brooks. Draymond Green questions Kendrick Perkins’ basketball intelligence Perkins had criticised Green during an appearance on ESPN’s First Take, questioning whether his focus had shifted away from basketball and towards on-court confrontations. He also pointed to Green’s lack of production early in the season, suggesting the Warriors were not getting enough from the four-time All-Star. Perkins said: “Listen, when was the last time we discussed Draymond Green and brought him up for his basketball and not fighting? At some point, he has to deliver on the floor. When you look at the start of this season, Draymond Green has been non-existent.” He added: “He has done absolutely nothing for the Golden State Warriors. To me, he has been a liability more than an asset.” Green responded on his podcast, The Draymond Green Show, admitting that his physical abilities have declined while taking aim at Perkins’ own playing career. The Warriors star said: “Kendrick Perkins said Draymond Green is a liability, he ain’t no asset no more. And guess what Kendrick Perkins … at 36-years-old, to be 37 this year, I am 1000 percent not the player I once was … I’m not even close to the player I once was.” He continued: “But, Kendrick Perkins, the difference between myself and big dummies like you is I can think. And so when your body didn’t move the same no more, you weren’t as athletic as you once were, it looked a little different for you cause you weren’t the smartest basketball player.” Green’s early-season numbers give Perkins’ criticism some context. Across six appearances, he is averaging 3.2 points, 5.0 rebounds and 6.3 assists per game, while shooting 38.9 per cent from the field. His latest ejection came after he forcefully brought Maluach to the floor, prompting Brooks to step in and confront him. Green later defended the play, arguing that a centre must stand up for himself to maintain respect around the basket. The Warriors have won five consecutive games after opening the season with three defeats, and Green will now be under pressure to turn his response into more consistent performances on the court. The Penguins ' losing streak reached four games on Thursday night with a 6-2 defeat at the hands of the Bruins, leaving Pittsburgh with a lot of questions and no easy answers. top.title: Blackhawks Lose 4-1 To Lightning, Now Dropped Five Straight Games
top.description: The Chicago Blackhawks (4-12-1) lost for the second time in as many nights and for the fifth game in a row on Thursday, falling 4-1 to the Tampa Bay Lightning (10-3-2) at Benchmark International Arena. The Blackhawks remain winless on the road this season, dropping to 0-7-1 in eight games. The Lightning remain undefeated at home, moving to 8-0-0. Former Blackhawks forward Ilya Mikheyev scored twice, including the game-winning goal, in his first game against his old team since signing with Tampa Bay in free agency this past summer. Victor Hedman (PP) and Ryan McDonagh also scored for the Lightning. McDonagh had a plus-three rating, while his defensive partner, Erik Cernak, added two assists with a plus-three rating. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 25 of 26 shots and has now won 15 of 16 career regular-season games against the Blackhawks. He’s allowed just 33 goals in those 16 games. Roman Kantserov was the only reason Vasilevskiy didn’t record his second career shutout against the Blackhawks, with the rookie snapping his fellow countryman’s shutout bid with 48.1 seconds left in the third period. It was Kantserov’s team-leading eighth goal of the season, which extended his current point streak to seven games. Sam Rinzel and Ethan Del Mastro tallied assists on the goal, marking back-to-back games with assists for both defensemen. Arvid Soderblom made his fourth start of the season and stopped 31 of 35 shots. Soderblom remains winless in 2026-27. For the second straight game, the Blackhawks fell behind 2-0 in the first period and never recovered. While they rallied for three goals in the final 40 minutes on Wednesday, there wasn’t much of an offensive pushback in the second and third periods against Tampa Bay. The Blackhawks registered only nine high-danger scoring chances in 60 minutes, as they struggled to find time and space with possession against the Lightning defense. They’ve now scored two goals or fewer in 11 of 17 games this season. Perhaps the only positive from Thursday’s loss was the Blackhawks increased physicality, leading 31-13 in hits. One night ago, the Hawks had only 12 hits and were pushed around in a 5-3 loss to the Florida Panthers. Scrappy fourth-liner Dillon Boucher led the team with seven hits in 8:12 of ice time, while also getting into a must-see scrap, his first NHL fight, against Jeff Viel in the second period. Boucher’s linemate, Cole Smith, was one of the better Blackhawks in Tampa and chipped in with six hits. That’s a significant step in the right direction for the Blackhawks in that aspect. Now, they just have to figure out how to score and keep the puck out of their own net… Here are highlights from the Blackhawks 4-1 loss in Tampa Bay. Anthony Cirelli found a soft spot between Frank Nazar and Alex Vlasic on the entry, then found Hedman streaking to the net for his fourth goal of the season.

nigeria.title: Atiku Verdict: APC wants opposition fighting – Ameh
nigeria.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — High Chief Peter Ameh, the National Democratic Congress (NDC) senatorial candidate for Kogi East, has warned opposition parties against celebrating the court judgment that sacked the David Mark-led National Working Committee of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and nullified Atiku Abubakar’s candidacy. Ameh said the ruling should not be seen as a victory for any political camp, warning that the All Progressives Congress (APC) stood to benefit from divisions within the opposition. He spoke in Abuja on Thursday, urging opposition parties to resist attempts to turn the judgment into an opportunity for political infighting. According to him, the APC would be comfortable with any opposition party being weakened, regardless of the party’s identity or political affiliation. “The APC, which is the ultimate beneficiary of this judgment, will be happy keeping any party in the opposition weakened. They do not care which party logo you wave. They want us fighting each other so we never notice the real game being played against all of us,” he said. Ameh cautioned that what might appear to be a victory for one faction today could become a tool against another political group tomorrow. “Before anyone starts dancing, remember: today’s victory for one camp is tomorrow’s weapon against another. The same forces that can erase one candidate or one leadership structure can just as easily turn on yours when it becomes convenient. Political affiliation is not a shield,” he said. He added: “Stay alert. This is not a win for any side. It is a warning.” The NDC candidate urged opposition parties to channel their energy towards demanding free, fair and credible elections, rather than engaging in disputes over political leadership and candidacies. He also criticised the APC-led administration, accusing it of failing to deliver good governance to Nigerians over the past 11 years. “For 11 years, this APC government has failed to provide good governance to Nigerians. We must collectively work to bring an end to its rule. APC is the problem,” Ameh declared. The post Atiku Verdict: APC wants opposition fighting – Ameh appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Benue SEMA raises alarm over rising snakebites, treats two IDPs
nigeria.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Benue State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA) has expressed concern over rising cases of snakebites across the state, warning that the incidents are increasingly affecting farmers, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and other vulnerable residents. The concern followed two recent snakebite incidents involving a 35-year-old man, Isaac Shula, and a 19-year-old girl, Mbapuun Tyoshio, both residents of Daudu 1 IDP camp in Guma Local Government Area of the state. The victims were reportedly bitten by snakes while working on their farms and have since been referred to the Benue State University Teaching Hospital (BSUTH), Makurdi, where they are receiving medical attention under the care of Benue SEMA. The agency’s Health Focal Person, Dr Amos Dzungwe, said snakebite cases had continued to increase across the state, affecting not only displaced persons but also farmers and other vulnerable populations. He said the agency had received numerous requests for medical intervention from different parts of the state, reflecting growing concern over the incidents. According to him, two snakebite patients were successfully discharged within the last two weeks, while others remained on admission and were receiving treatment. Dzungwe warned against delays in seeking medical attention, stressing that late presentation at health facilities could result in severe complications and poor health outcomes. He urged members of the public to seek immediate medical attention at appropriate health facilities whenever snakebite incidents occur. Meanwhile, Benue SEMA has urged the public to disregard what it described as misleading reports and politically motivated narratives surrounding snakebite incidents in the state, particularly those involving IDPs. The agency maintained that health emergencies and the lives of vulnerable citizens should not be subjected to political manipulation. nigeria.title: LASTMA inducts 100 volunteers to tackle Yuletide traffic
nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) has inducted more than 100 volunteers into its LASTMA Mayors traffic advocacy network to support efforts to manage anticipated traffic congestion during the Yuletide and year-end ‘Detty December’ celebrations. The investiture and induction ceremony, held at the agency’s headquarters in Lagos, was part of efforts to strengthen community participation in traffic management, promote voluntary compliance with traffic regulations and support enforcement officers along busy roads. Speaking at the event, LASTMA General Manager, Olalekan Bakare-Oki, said managing traffic in Lagos required collective responsibility rather than reliance on government enforcement alone. Bakare-Oki cautioned motorists against dangerous practices, including driving against traffic, popularly known as one-way, excessive speeding, reckless overtaking and indiscriminate parking. He also urged vehicle owners to ensure proper maintenance of their brakes, tyres, steering systems and lights before embarking on journeys. “The commercial excitement and social festivities associated with December must not degenerate into traffic indiscipline or preventable road tragedies,” he said, urging motorists to exercise patience and restraint. nigeria.title: Soludo seeks partnership with pharmacists to strengthen healthcare
nigeria.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for a strategic partnership between the state government and the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) to strengthen the healthcare system and improve access to quality pharmaceutical services. Soludo made the call on Wednesday while declaring open the ongoing four-day 99th Annual National Delegate Conference of the society in Awka, stressing that pharmacists played a critical role in building an effective healthcare system. Describing the gathering, tagged ‘Ijele 2026’, as historic, the governor said his administration had prioritised human capital development, education and healthcare. He cited the introduction of free education from kindergarten to Senior Secondary School Three (SS3), as well as free antenatal care in government hospitals, as part of his administration’s interventions in the sectors. Soludo also said his government had revamped the state’s primary healthcare system, disclosing that more than 250,000 expectant mothers had benefited from zero-cost antenatal care, while over 950 free Caesarean Section operations had been performed. “To further solidify Anambra’s position as the nation’s premier pharma hub, let me also inform you that work on the development of the state-of-the-art Pharmaceutical Hub in Oba, alongside the upcoming Coordinated Wholesale Centre slated for delivery early next year, is currently ongoing in the state,” he said. The governor urged the PSN leadership to work closely with the state government to enforce safety standards in pharmaceutical operations and tackle the circulation of counterfeit drugs. He also challenged the society to address unethical practices within the profession, particularly the activities of illegal drug outlets operating under the guise of licensed pharmacies. Earlier, the President of the PSN, Pharm. Ayuba Tanko Ibrahim, expressed appreciation to Soludo for his support for the pharmaceutical profession and the decision to host the society’s flagship national conference in Anambra. nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — The Society of Women Accountants of Nigeria (SWAN) has identified poor financial record-keeping, inadequate cash flow management, ineffective pricing and limited understanding of profitability as some of the factors undermining the survival and growth of businesses in Nigeria. The association said many promising businesses struggle not necessarily because of a lack of opportunities or customers, but because their owners lack the financial knowledge required to manage resources and make informed decisions. SWAN stated this at its 2026 Accounting for Non-Accountants Workshop, held on Thursday at the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN) Annex, Ebute-Metta, Lagos. The workshop, organised as part of the association’s Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives, had the theme, “Business Made Easy: Practical Financial Skills.” Speaking at the event, Chairperson of the Planning Committee, Mrs Ruth Jawo, said financial literacy had become essential for entrepreneurs, traders, professionals, employees and business managers, particularly amid the country’s challenging economic conditions. According to her, financial knowledge would enable business owners to make informed decisions, manage resources effectively, avoid penalties and achieve sustainable growth. “The theme reflects SWAN’s commitment to simplifying financial concepts and equipping participants with practical knowledge,” she said. Jawo explained that the workshop was designed to bridge existing financial knowledge gaps and empower participants to manage their finances more confidently. She expressed the expectation that participants would apply the knowledge acquired to improve their businesses, workplaces and households. “Our expectation is that every participant leaves with valuable knowledge, practical tools and a renewed determination to develop better financial habits. “The true success of this workshop will be measured not merely by attendance, but by the positive changes it inspires in businesses, workplaces and households,” she said. nigeria.title: $2bn Afreximbank fund targets Africa’s creative economy as CANEX opens in Lagos
nigeria.description: By Elizabeth Onyogha Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) WKND 2026 opened in Lagos yesterday, bringing together leading creatives, investors, policymakers, business leaders and cultural figures from across Africa and the diaspora to explore investment, financing and commercial opportunities in the continent’s creative economy. Hosted by the Federal Government of Nigeria and organised by the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) through its Creative Africa Nexus programme, the four-day event runs from November 5 to 8 under the theme, “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World.” The programme covers film and television, music, fashion, sport, literature and publishing, gastronomy and visual arts, with emphasis on financing, intellectual property, technology, skills development, investment and market access. Through platforms such as the CANEX Deal Room and Creative Pitch Sessions, the event seeks to connect entrepreneurs with financiers and investors, turning creative ideas and talent into viable businesses, partnerships and commercial opportunities. The initiative builds on Afreximbank’s commitment to Africa’s creative and cultural industries, which began in 2020 and has since expanded to $2 billion in available financing. The funding is designed to help African creators and businesses develop scalable enterprises, strengthen ownership of intellectual property and retain more of the economic value generated by the continent’s cultural and creative industries. nigeria.title: REA flags off 18.8MW mini-grid projects to connect 125,106 Zamfara households

The projects, comprising two interconnected and 35 isolated mini-grids, are expected to connect 125,106 households across Gummi, Gusau, Kaura Namoda, Maradun, Shinkafi, Tsafe and Zurmi Local Government Areas. The groundbreaking ceremony on Wednesday also featured the unveiling of the Zamfara State Electricity Policy and the signing of a collaboration agreement between REA and the state government for the solarisation of public institutions. nigeria.title: Malaria, TB Diagnosis: Global Fund Trains 464 Lab personnel in 9 States
nigeria.description: … Experts say poor tests fuel malaria misdiagnosis By Chioma Obinna Poor laboratory testing, inaccurate malaria diagnosis and unnecessary prescription of antimalarial drugs remain major challenges undermining Nigeria’s fight against malaria, health experts have warned. The experts spoke as the Global Fund supported the training of 464 laboratory personnel across nine states to strengthen malaria and tuberculosis (TB) diagnosis, improve disease surveillance and ensure reliable laboratory results. The integrated capacity-building programme, implemented through the National Malaria Elimination Programme (NMEP) and the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, was inaugurated at Mokland Hotel, Ibara, GRA, Abeokuta, Ogun State. Speaking at the event, Consultant Medical Parasitologist, College of Medicine, University of Lagos, Professor Wellington Oyibo, said accurate diagnosis was critical to effective treatment, warning that laboratory personnel must be equipped to identify different malaria parasite species and distinguish infections from other illnesses. He said microscopy remained essential despite the availability of rapid diagnostic tests and molecular technologies, stressing the need for quality assurance, proper documentation and timely reporting. Oyibo said participants would be trained in slide preparation, microscopy, parasite identification, quality management and diagnostic best practices, including standards under ISO 15189. He said the programme was designed to produce a critical mass of competent laboratory professionals who would also mentor colleagues in their respective facilities. In a troubling revelation, Ogun State Malaria Elimination Programme Manager, Mrs Olamide Adeyinka, said patients’ insistence on having malaria despite negative test results was contributing to inappropriate treatment and unreliable malaria statistics. She explained that some patients pressured health workers into prescribing antimalarial drugs even when laboratory investigations showed otherwise. She said, “We have always recorded a high malaria test positivity rate, but many of these cases are linked to the failure to conduct proper tests or patients refusing to accept test results.” Adeyinka disclosed that participants were drawn from all 20 local government areas of Ogun State, covering primary, secondary and tertiary health facilities, as well as private and faith-based institutions. Also, Assistant Director, Medical Laboratory Services, Ogun State, Dr Simon Ijiezie, warned that inaccurate diagnosis was exposing people without malaria to unnecessary medication and financial losses. He appealed to the state government to provide quality laboratory equipment, particularly microscopes, to ensure that the training translates into improved services. “Without a good microscope, accurate diagnosis becomes difficult,” he said. nigeria.title: 2027: Tinubu, T. Y. Danjuma, Northeast, North-Central leaders meet in Aso Villa
nigeria.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru Ahead of January 16, 2027 presidential election, the former Minister of Defence, General Theophilus Danjuma (retd) and political leaders from the Northeast and North-Central geopolitical zones yesterday, met behind closed doors with President Bola Tinubu at the Aso Villa, Abuja. The meeting it was gathered was part of have consultations aimed at mobilising support for the President. nigeria.title: Bournemouth stay perfect in Europa League as Milan lose again
nigeria.description: Bournemouth extended their perfect Europa League record on Thursday as they came from behind to win 3-1 at 10-man Sparta Prague, while Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan suffered a third defeat in four matches. Gambian Ebrima Singhateh ran from his own half to score a fine individual goal as Sparta took the lead in the Czech Republic after Bournemouth midfielder Lewis Cook hit the post with a first-half penalty. Sparta had Tobias Guddal sent off before half-time and Bournemouth equalised through Tyler Adams on 57 minutes. Evanilson steered the Cherries ahead nine minutes from time and Rayan bagged a late third as Bournemouth’s substitutes sent the European newcomers top of the table with a fourth successive victory. Marco Rose’s side have won each of their past seven matches in all competitions ahead of a Premier League trip to Ipswich this weekend. “It’s a big achievement and we have to continue, we need to stay alert, sharp,” Rose told TNT Sports. “It’s up to us to use this momentum. Everyone tries to beat us, if we get in a comfort zone just a little bit we get in trouble.” Milan lost 2-0 at home to Ferencvaros as the Hungarians kept pace with Bournemouth, maintaining their 100 percent record in Europe. Haiti international Lenny Joseph struck twice in the second half at San Siro to earn Ferencvaros a deserved win over the seven-time European champions despite having Bamidele Yusuf sent off. “We gifted opportunities, made stupid errors. We were not prepared to play football tonight,” Amorim told Sky Sport. “I don’t want to lie to my players. We cannot play like this in front of our own fans. It was a very poor performance.” Milan are languishing outside the top 24 with just three points at the halfway stage of the league phase. “I won’t give up on this competition. As long as we’re not mathematically out of it, we’ll keep fighting,” Amorim added. Crystal Palace snatched a 1-1 draw at home to Hoffenheim as Japanese midfielder Daichi Kamada levelled in stoppage time. Alexander Prass gave Hoffenheim an early lead at Selhurst Park and Palace lost Adam Wharton to a second yellow card before Kamada rescued a point for Pierre Sage’s struggling side. Palace, last season’s UEFA Conference League winners, have five points from four outings in the Europa League but sit in the Premier League’s relegation zone, just behind Manchester United on goal difference. nigeria.title: Ebola patient flown to UK from DR Congo
nigeria.description: A UK medic who tested positive for Ebola while working on the outbreak of the disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been flown to London for treatment, the government said Thursday. The unnamed British citizen “has returned to the UK for specialist treatment after testing positive for the disease”, the government said in a statement. Africa’s latest Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,300 people, the vast majority of them in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to the continent’s top health agency. The British government said that the UK medic is now being treated at the Royal Free Hospital in London. This hospital has a high-level isolation unit “specifically designed for this purpose” and strict protocols to prevent contact with the general public, it said. Renu Bindra, deputy director of the all hazards public health response team at the UK health security agency (UKHSA) said “the risk to the wider public remains low”. Last month, Nigeria reported an Ebola case involving a 42-year-old Swiss woman whose husband works at the country’s embassy. She was flown for treatment in Geneva. nigeria.title: 2027: Peter Obi Has Not Offered Any Alternative — Oshiomhole
nigeria.description: The Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has not offered any alternative to the policies of President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Oshiomhole described Obi as a trader whose approach, according to him, focuses on short-term gains rather than long-term national development. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I think it is you or someone else who asked him for security, what will you do differently? He said, it’s in his heart. “I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” he said. ﻿ Oshiomhole said he respected the right of opposition candidates to contest for the presidency but believed Tinubu should remain in office after “having gone through all the teething problems” rather than “recruit a new apprentice.” He also criticised the record of the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, under which former Vice President Atiku Abubakar served, alleging that they were unable to guarantee the payment of workers’ salaries. The Edo North Senator said the 2027 presidential election would present Nigerians with a choice between Tinubu, whom he credited with unifying the exchange rate, and Atiku, whose administration he accused of allowing different exchange rates for people based on their connections. Oshiomhole also defended the Tinubu administration’s handling of workers’ welfare, saying the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 transport allowance showed that the President cared about them. “I think this government is doing well. If a man who was on ₦70,000 now is given ₦70,000 addition that makes it ₦140,000 for him it’s a hundred percent increase and if you know what ₦10,000 means for the real masses, you’ll appreciate that Tinubu has shown that he cares,” Oshiomhole said. The Federal Government approved the monthly ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a meeting with the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on October 27. The agreement also provides for the payment of outstanding peculiar allowances in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. However, the Trade Union Congress (TUC) rejected the transport allowance, arguing that workers need a permanent salary increase rather than temporary relief. nigeria.title: ADC Court Ruling: ‘APC Afraid Of Strong Candidate Against Tinubu’ – Osunbor
nigeria.description: A former Governor of Edo State and National Legal Adviser of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Oserheimen Osunbor, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of being jittery ahead of the January 2027 presidential election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Osunbor said the APC did not want a strong candidate to challenge President Bola Tinubu at the polls. “I have said that repeatedly, they (APC) are afraid of any strong candidate running against President Bola Tinubu in the January presidential election,” Osunbor said. ﻿ The ADC legal adviser said the party and its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, were continuing with their campaigns because they believed the court judgment nullifying Atiku’s candidacy would not stand. “Our presidential candidate (Atiku Abubakar) and the presidential campaign is going on, unperturbed because we believe that this judgment will not stand and cannot stand,” he said. nigeria.title: Traders attack Edo Consumer Protection Committee members over fake products
nigeria.description: By Ozioruva Aliu – BENIN CITY Member of the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee led by its chairman, Osaro Culture Iyamu were, on Thursday, attacked by some beverage sellers while trying to enforce ban on sales of fake, adulterated and unauthorised drinks along Mission Road in Benin City, the state capital. nigeria.title: Nigeria must deploy tollgates, technology to improve highway security – Musa
nigeria.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa (retd), has advocated restoring tollgates on major highways and deploying modern technology to enhance highway security and help identify and track criminals. Musa noted that tollgates could play a valuable security role, especially with modern technology that can identify and track vehicles without requiring drivers to stop for manual payments. The minister made the remarks at the Abuja roundtable, “Promise to Proof: The Renewed Hope Conversation,” organised by the APC Progressive Strategy Roundtable. It was convened by the Executive Chairman/CEO of PICNG and EVs, Ismaeel Ahmed. Responding to concerns about highway security and a suggestion that motorists could contribute through security levies at tollgates, Musa described the reintroduction of tollgates as a good idea, noting that Nigeria might have made a mistake by dismantling them. He explained that modern tolling systems in other countries use technology to identify vehicles through their registration numbers, with payments processed electronically, adding that such systems could also assist security agencies in identifying and tracking vehicles. The minister also called for the strengthening of Nigeria’s identification system through the use of personal identification numbers, facial recognition and fingerprints to improve security monitoring. He said technology would make it easier for security agencies to establish people’s identities and track criminal activities. On the broader security situation, Musa said the Federal Government was recording progress in tackling terrorism, banditry and kidnapping through increased defence investment, improved intelligence gathering, joint military operations and stronger cooperation among security agencies. He disclosed that the Federal Government allocated ₦5.4 trillion to defence in the 2026 budget and was recruiting an additional 12,000 military personnel to strengthen manpower and security coverage. According to him, the government was also investing in modern weapons, surveillance systems and operational platforms to improve intelligence gathering, mobility, firepower and rapid response capabilities. He further disclosed that Nigerian security forces killed more than 300 terrorists and bandits, including over 10 commanders, in operations conducted in the week preceding his presentation. The minister identified porous borders as a major challenge, noting that Nigeria shares extensive borders with neighbouring countries, particularly Niger Republic, through which criminal groups and illicit arms can move. He said the government was strengthening border security and expanding bilateral, regional and international defence cooperation through intelligence sharing, specialised training and technological support. nigeria.title: Italian chef sacked for refusing to put pineapple on pizza, says it insulted his culture
nigeria.description: An Italian chef in Australia has lost an unfair dismissal claim after being sacked for, among other workplace issues, refusing to serve ham and pineapple pizza, describing the topping as an insult to his culture. Davide Tamburella was dismissed from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in Brisbane in May, following a meeting with management over several complaints about his conduct. One of the issues raised was his refusal to prepare ham and pineapple pizzas for guests attending an event at the restaurant. According to a ruling by Australia’s Fair Work Commission, Tamburella argued that instructions from management “need not be followed when it is offensive to his culture”. The commission noted that the chef’s objection to the fruit was because “he considers, as an Italian, that putting pineapple on a pizza is an insult to his culture”. nigeria.description: By Joseph Erunke The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has moved to tighten its grip on the conduct of the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME), warning that computer-based test (CBT) centres that fail to meet its prescribed standards will be denied accreditation. The Board said the accreditation exercise would serve as a critical screening mechanism to prevent inadequately equipped centres from participating in the examination, thereby protecting candidates from avoidable disruptions and compromising examination conditions. Reiterating its position, JAMB declared that accreditation would not be automatic for CBT centres seeking to participate in the exercise. “Only centres that meet JAMB’s standards will be accredited to host the examination. For candidates, that means a fair and secure place to sit the UTME, wherever they write it,” the Board stated. The development signals JAMB’s determination to strengthen the credibility of the UTME by ensuring that candidates, irrespective of their examination locations, have access to a secure, reliable and conducive testing environment. The strict accreditation regime is also expected to address operational shortcomings that have historically threatened the smooth conduct of computer-based examinations, including inadequate facilities and poor technical readiness. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Greece Approves 10% Crypto Capital Gains Tax as First Framework Lands Below Draft Rate Greece’s parliament approved on Thursday a bill that imposes a 10% capital gains tax on cryptocurrencies, the first comprehensive legal framework for taxing crypto assets in the country. Cryptocurrency capital gains of up to €500 ($563) a year will be exempt from the new tax, the bill says. For bitcoin holders in Greece, that threshold is a small buffer, not a carve-out for larger positions. “Further implementation directives will be published in the coming weeks, which will also define transparency and audit rules,” a senior finance ministry official told Reuters . An earlier draft circulated in October had floated a 15% rate. The version lawmakers passed lands five points lower, while keeping the €500 annual exemption that was already in that proposal. What the levy covers for bitcoin holders The tax is set to apply from Jan. 1, 2027, Greek coverage of the finance ministry bill says. It is levied on the net gain — the difference between the acquisition price and the transfer price — not on the full sale proceeds. Trading fees and other costs tied to the deal can factor into that calculation. A taxable transfer is not limited to selling for euros. Using cryptocurrency to buy goods or services, or contributing it to cover or increase company capital, can also crystallize a gain under the new rules. That matters for anyone in Greece who pays a merchant in bitcoin rather than converting first. Simply holding bitcoin while its euro value rises does not, by itself, create a tax bill. Crypto-to-crypto swaps, such as bitcoin for another token, are treated as non-taxable events in the explanatory material that accompanied the bill, matching the approach France has used to avoid taxing every hop between coins. Net annual gains at or below €500 are exempt. Greek analyses of the text say that once net gains clear that ceiling, the 10% rate applies to the full net gain for the year, not only the slice above €500. Losses above €500 in a tax year may be carried forward for up to five years and offset only against future crypto capital gains. Purchases of crypto assets are also being pulled into Greece’s existing “source of funds” checks from 2027, so buyers may need to show that the euros used to acquire bitcoin or other tokens came from declared income or other lawful capital. The rule does not add a separate purchase tax; it widens the audit trail around how coins were funded. Rates on cryptocurrency gains typically run from about 8% to 30% across member states and are usually levied on capital gains, the finance ministry official said. entertainment.title: iDICE Named Official Deal Room Partner for Afreximbank’s CANEX WKND 2026
entertainment.description: The Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) Programme, a US$617 million initiative of the Federal Government of Nigeria implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), will take part in Afreximbank’s Creative Africa Nexus Weekend (CANEX WKND 2026) as one of the event’s official Deal Room Partner. The US$617 million programme is implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI), which also co-finances it alongside the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB). It backs young Nigerians aged 15–35 and the businesses they build in the technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance and enabling infrastructure. CANEX WKND 2026 holds from 5 to 8 November 2026 in Lagos under the theme “One People, United in Culture, Creating for the World,” bringing together creatives, investors, financial institutions, policymakers and development partners from across Africa and the diaspora. At the heart of iDICE’s participation is the iDICE Deal Room, which will host structured meetings between 15–20 investment-ready creative and digital enterprises and investors and financiers, including iDICE-backed fund managers Ventures Platform and Kuramo Capital, the BOI-iDICE Debt Fund, the BOI Non-Interest Banking team managing the IsDB-supported facility, and participating financial institutions. The Deal Room aims to hold 40–50 investor–enterprise meetings and generate investment leads for follow-up after the event. iDICE and BOI will also take part in high-level sessions on financing and technology in the creative economy, and showcase programme-supported enterprises at the iDICE exhibition stand. “Nigeria’s digital and creative industries hold significant potential to drive economic growth, create jobs, expand exports and strengthen the country’s global competitiveness. Realising this potential requires sustained investment in enterprise development, access to finance and the capabilities of our young people. Through the iDICE Programme, the Federal Government and the Bank of Industry are working with development partners to address these needs and build a stronger ecosystem for digital and creative enterprises. CANEX WKND provides an important platform to deepen engagement with industry stakeholders, connect creative entrepreneurs to investment opportunities and advance the partnerships needed to grow the sector,”said Ife Adebayo . The National Coordinator of the iDICE Programme, Ife Adebayo, added: “The Deal Room is about turning conversations into investment. We are bringing some of the most promising enterprises from the iDICE pipeline to meet financiers ready to back them, while showing what iDICE is already delivering for young Nigerian founders and creatives.” Creative and tech entrepreneurs attending CANEX WKND 2026 are invited to visit the iDICE Exhibition stand to learn about available financing and support, including non-interest financing

Consulate General Lagos recently recognized the contributions of Lagos Fashion Week founder Omoyemi Akerele at a lunch held at the height of Lagos Fashion Week 2026. The event recognized Akerele’s vision in connecting Nigerian designers with American consumers and creating new opportunities for U.S. businesses. The occasion brought together designers, entrepreneurs, and creative leaders to highlight fashion’s role in strengthening U.S.-Nigeria ties. “It’s an honor to celebrate Lagos Fashion Week 2026 with so many of Nigeria’s most talented designers and creative leaders. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. entertainment.title: Ejiro Amos Tafiri Unveils REVERIE, Its Spring/Summer 2027 Collection, Celebrating Reinvention in African Luxury
entertainment.description: Ejiro Amos Tafiri , a Pan-African luxury fashion house founded in Lagos in 2010, has unveiled REVERIE, its Spring/Summer 2027 (SS27) collection, at an exclusive private showcase in Lagos on Sunday, October 25, 2026, held alongside Lagos Fashion Week. The showcase brought together distinguished guests, fashion industry leaders, patrons and representatives of the British Council Nigeria, including chef and media personality Hilda Baci, for a presentation of the house’s latest collection. REVERIE explores renewal and reinvention through contemporary African luxury. Bringing together expressive silhouettes, intricate craftsmanship and a refined colour palette, the collection presents a visual statement that celebrates the evolving language of African fashion. Through considered design and craftsmanship, REVERIE reflects the house’s continued exploration of contemporary African aesthetics, presenting pieces that balance creative expression with the distinctive design sensibility for which Ejiro Amos Tafiri is known. Founded by designer Ejiro Amos Tafiri, known for her signature Drapes, the fashion house has spent 16 years developing a distinctive identity within the luxury fashion landscape. Its design language is characterized by expressive drapery, fluid tailoring and the thoughtful use of indigenous textiles, bringing African craftsmanship into contemporary fashion. The Lagos unveiling followed the third edition of Fashioning a Legacy: Leaving a Mark in Time, held on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at the British Council in Ikoyi, Lagos. The conference brought together designers, stylists, retail professionals and emerging creatives to discuss building sustainable careers and creating lasting impact within the fashion industry. Together, the events reflect Ejiro Amos Tafiri’s continued engagement with the broader creative ecosystem, connecting fashion, education, craftsmanship and the development of emerging talent. The REVERIE presentation forms part of the house’s 16-year milestone and will be followed by an exclusive showcase in Abuja on November 21, 2026. The forthcoming event will bring together members of the diplomatic community, government officials, fashion patrons and invited guests for a further presentation of the house’s work. entertainment.title: Pan-African School Games 2026: Celebrating Young Talent, School Pride and New Opportunities
entertainment.description: The Pan-African School Games 2026 brought together young athletes from schools across Lagos for three days of swimming, athletics and football, celebrating sporting talent, school pride and the opportunities that organized competition can create for children and young people. Held at James Hope College, Lekki, from 16 to 18 October, the second edition of the Games featured the U-11, U-13 and U-15 categories. Students competed for individual honours and school points while gaining valuable experience in a structured, multi-sport environment. The competition also welcomed sporting stakeholders and scouts, reinforcing the wider ambition of the Pan-African School Games: to give young athletes a platform where their abilities can be demonstrated, recognized and developed. Building on the Inaugural Games The second edition of the Pan-African School Games built on the foundation established by the inaugural Games in 2025, continuing the vision of creating meaningful sporting opportunities for young athletes. The 2026 edition welcomed schools and student-athletes for three days of swimming, athletics and football, providing a platform for competition, talent development and school pride. Beyond the sporting results, the Games continued to advance a broader ambition: to connect schools, athletes, sporting stakeholders and educational institutions while creating opportunities for young people to develop their abilities and explore future pathways through sport. Day One: Swimming Opens the Games Swimming opened the competition, bringing young swimmers together for races across the U-11, U-13 and U-15 categories. The opening day set the pace for the Games as athletes took to the pool to test their abilities, pursue strong performances and earn points for their schools. The races highlighted the preparation, discipline and technique required to compete, while providing young swimmers with valuable experience in a formal sporting environment. For many of the students, the opportunity to compete alongside athletes from other schools added to the significance of the experience. Each race contributed to the overall competition, with schools beginning their campaigns for medals and category honours. Day Two: Athletics Puts Young Athletes to the Test Athletics took centre stage on the second day, with track and field events testing the speed, strength, coordination and technique of the young competitors. Athletes competed in running, jumping and throwing events, earning points for their schools as the standings developed. Each discipline presented a different challenge, giving students opportunities to demonstrate their abilities and compete for individual and team honours. The athletics programme added another dimension to the Games, highlighting the variety of talent within the participating schools and the value of giving young athletes opportunities to develop through competition. entertainment.title: African Philanthropy Leaders Call for Bolder, Locally Led Giving at the 2026 APF Conference in Cape Town
entertainment.description: CAPE TOWN, South Africa: African Philanthropy Forum (APF) closed its 2026 Conference in Cape Town on 27 October with a message that ran through nearly every session: Africa’s challenges are connected, so African giving has to be connected too. Held from 25 to 27 October under the theme Bridge the Divide; Reimagine the Future , the conference brought together philanthropists, funders, business leaders, creatives, and technologists to ask how African capital can be mobilized, how partnerships can be strengthened, and how African-led solutions can be backed with more trust and flexibility. Centered on Africa, the program also looked outward, drawing on solutions from across the Global South and asking how African philanthropy can bridge the divide. The conference opened on Sunday evening with a reception at Cape Point Vineyards, where Executive Director Mosun Layode welcomed delegates, members and acknowledged APF Board members, including Chair Gbenga Oyebode , Wale Adeosun , and Nyimpini Mabunda . Former Board Member Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa urged guests to look past the continent’s challenges and toward its potential and to use the days ahead to turn conversations into partnerships. It was an evening of connection before two days of ideas at the Norval Foundation. Reimagining the Future Monday, 26 October, began with a call to build bridges across regions, languages, and funding silos. Mosun Layode and Gbenga Oyebode officially opened and welcomed all delegates to the conference. Dr. Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka , former Vice President of South Africa, spoke of education as a sacred right of every African child and of bringing young people into decision-making. In the first keynote, Gary Lubner, Founder of the This Day Foundation, described giving away 95 percent of his wealth during his lifetime and said it was easier and more joyful than holding it for heirs. Old money thinking, he argued, is a major barrier to giving, and generosity includes time and effort as well as cash. The numbers framed the challenge. Delegates heard that Africa needs about $1.3 trillion in financing each year, while philanthropy contributes $5 billion to $6 billion. The task is to use that small pool to unlock far larger sources, such as pension funds and fixed-income assets, so money reaches businesses that create jobs. In an afternoon keynote moderated by Marlene Ogawa of Synergos, Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa , South Africa CEO of Naspers, and Gareth Ackerman, Non-Executive Director at Pick n Pay, kept things practical: back women entrepreneurs without taking equity, start with your own family and community, use local distributors, and make it easier to travel between African countries. One retraining program they discussed moved 7,200 of 8,000 university graduates into tech jobs. The difference between charity and philanthropy, they said, is helping people help themselves. sports.description: ELMONT, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 05: Brandon Bussi #32 of the Carolina Hurricanes saves a shot from Anthony Duclair #11 of the New York Islanders during the first period at UBS Arena on November 05, 2026 in Elmont, New York. (Photo by Steven Ryan/NHLI via Getty Images) | NHLI via Getty Images According to coach Rod Brind’Amour the team was “not at its best”, but the Carolina Hurricanes scored twice in the third period and held on to defeat the New York Islanders, 5-3 on Thursday night at UBS Arena. The Canes improved their record to 13-3-2 on the season. Brandon Bussi made 24 saves on the 27 shots he faced to pick up his third win of the season. Logan Stankoven got things started just 57 seconds into the game when he took a pass from Jackson Blake and ripped it past goalie Semyon Varlamov. Stankoven now has a team leading 11 goals for the season. Blake added to his team-high assist total to 14. A couple of minutes later, Jesperi Kotkaniemi tipped in a Jordan Martinook pass to make it 2-0 and it looked like Carolina was flying. But they took their feet off the gas and the Islanders got back in the game. The home team tied the score at two but the Canes would strike again on an Andrei Svechnokov goal in the second. The Islanders tied it at three before the end of the period and even though the Canes were outshooting NY, they seemed to be reeling a bit. But they came out strong in the third period. Will Carrier knocked in the game-winner off a Svechnikov shot 15 minutes and change into the third and that would be enough to finish off the Islanders. Jalen Chatfield fought for a loose puck and put in a long shot into an empty net to complete the scoring. All in all, it was the team’s best effort but they did what they needed to do to get the win. Next up will be a game at home on Saturday night against the Blackhawks which will be their last game before the trip to Finland. Notes: Kotkaniemi had a team low 8 minutes of ice time. He now has 5 goals and 3 assists and has played well recently. Not sure what else he needs to do to see more ice time. He also had 2 hits and was 50% in the faceoff circle. Taylor Hall returned to action and played just over 10 minutes. The Canes went 34% in the circle. The Hurricanes ended up outshooting the home team, 39-27. sports.description: (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars won on Thursday night and moved up in the AFC standings. With the Pittsburgh Steelers on a bye, the Jags’ position will be at least third by the end of the weekend, and they can move into second and a tie for first place if everything goes their way. Let’s not get too far ahead of ourselves. Here are the standings as we stand now, then we will get into the rest of the weekend. AFC playoff standings after the Jaguars win 1. Buffalo Bills (6-1) 2. Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) Explaining the 6-2 tiebreaker between the Jaguars, Steelers, and Broncos The Jaguars, Broncos, and Steelers all go in together and while they will all play each other eventually, that hasn’t happened so we skip the head-to-head-to-head tiebreaker. The tiebreaker moves to conference record where the 3-1 Broncos best the 5-2 Jaguars and the 3-2 Steelers. Denver is the two seed. The Bills could lose to the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night to fall into that 6-2 tie, but they are 5-1 in the AFC and that isn’t going to change. The highest the Jaguars can get is second behind Buffalo — for now.

sports.title: Fort Defiance volleyball cruises to regional final
sports.description: After more than a week off, Fort Defiance showed no signs of rust in its playoff opener Nov. 5. The top seed in Region 2B rolled over No. 4 Clarke County 25-11, 25-10, 25-20 in the Region 2B semifinals. With the win, Fort Defiance will host No. 2 Madison County for the regional championship Nov. 10. Both teams have already earned a spot in the Class 2 state playoffs. Fort Defiance was on fire from the start. They didn't have a single serving or hitting error in the opening set, setting the tone for the night. The 75-minute match was short work for Fort, which is aiming to reach the state championship game for the third season in a row. Junior Caroline Hanger couldn't remember playing a set with no errors. "It was just great. Everything was just flowing," said Hanger, who finished with 10 kills. "All the hitters were doing so good and the defense was picking everything up." Freshman Maddie Gale had another all-around good game, finishing with six kills, 18 assists and four aces. Senior libero Norah Anderson had nine digs and four aces, while junior middle Harper Carter had six kills and sophomore Abbi Bright had seven digs and Alexis Miller added six assists in the win. "I think if we keep playing like how we played tonight, I feel confidence in our skills," said Hanger. sports.title: Kozo Tashima: Japan leader looking to bring 'integrity' to FIFA
sports.description: Kozo Tashima has announced he intends to run for the FIFA presidency (Toshifumi KITAMURA) Kozo Tashima first started playing football after watching the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, and since then he has dedicated his life to developing the sport's growth in Japan. The 68-year-old is set to become the first person from Japan to run for the FIFA presidency after announcing he would stand against Gianni Infantino in football's governing body's election in March. Tashima has served as a football player, coach and bureaucrat and has a reputation for being a safe pair of hands. He rarely makes headlines, and one of the few times he appeared outside the sport pages was when he became one of the first public figures in Japan to contract coronavirus in March 2020. He spent time studying at the German Sport University Cologne and said the experience changed the way he saw sport's purpose in society. He says his decision to run for the FIFA presidency was based on a belief that "in this age of business and money, sport must firmly uphold its integrity". "The worst thing would be if he (Infantino) were to continue without an election," he told reporters after announcing his candidacy. "I feel this is a test of whether FIFA has the ability to cleanse itself." Tashima was born in southern Kumamoto and captained his team to the title in Japan's prestigious national high school championship. With no professional football in the country at the time, he had ambitions of becoming a PE teacher and enrolled at a university, where he was called up to play for Japan's full national team. He joined a club in Japan's amateur league after graduating but soon retired as a player and went to Germany to study to become a coach. He described his "profound shock" at the players' superior skills and the way football was viewed there. "Even back in 1980, the training in Germany was hugely scientific and systematic," he said. "Everything seemed like a different world from Japan, and it was a big culture shock for me." - Experienced hand - Tashima returned home determined to use what he had learned in Germany and help develop Japanese football. He coached a university team before joining the Japan Football Association (JFA), where he worked on development programmes and coached the country's national teams at various youth levels. He rose through the JFA ranks and was elected president in 2016, while also serving on the Asian Football Confederation executive committee and the FIFA Council. His reign as JFA chief saw him fire Japan coach Vahid Halilhodzic two months before the 2018 World Cup in Russia. sports.title: ‘They have no shame’: Danny Kanell issues warning of 8-4 SEC team in College Football Playoff
sports.description: Sep 19, 2026; College Station, Texas, USA; The SEC logo seen on a down chain during the game between the Texas A&M Aggies and the Kentucky Wildcats at Kyle Field. Mandatory Credit: Maria Lysaker-Imagn Images The College Football Playoff selection committee caused quite a stir this week when it ranked two-loss Alabama No. 5 in its first rankings of the season. The decision left plenty of fans and analysts convinced that the SEC is getting the benefit of the doubt from the committee once again. Now, Danny Kanell is predicting things are going to get even worse. The former Florida State quarterback warned that there will be a push for an 8-4 SEC team to make the playoff this season. Alabama’s Controversial Ranking Alabama has losses to Georgia and Tennessee this season, including a 26-10 defeat in Knoxville on Oct. 17. Even so, the committee ranked the Crimson Tide at No. 5, making them one of the highest-ranked two-loss teams in College Football Playoff history. To make matters worse for critics, Tennessee came in all the way down at No. 13, outside of the playoff field. Texas, which beat Tennessee in that same stadium back in September, was ranked two spots behind Alabama at No. 7. The debate also comes as the playoff is set to grow even bigger. Last month, the CFP was reportedly nearing a deal to expand to 24 teams beginning in 2027, which Kanell supported. “I think this could be a great day for college football. I’m actually excited,” Kanell said at the time, on CBS Sports . ‘Brace Yourselves’ Needless to say, the decision to rank Alabama all the way at No. 5 received a lot of pushback. While a lot of the criticism was directed at Alabama specifically, Kanell took aim at the SEC as a whole, predicting an even bigger push for the conference this postseason. “I hope everyone is prepared for the push for an 8-4 SEC team in the college football playoff. Several pointed out that his support for a 24-team playoff would open the door for teams with even more losses. “As opposed to your 24-team CFP where they’ll push for a 7-5 SEC team – great work!” wrote Josh Pate , college football analyst for ESPN, On3, and Yahoo Sports. “you meant 5-7…7 good SEC losses – huge resume builders,” Kanell replied . “But with the 24 team CFP that’s gonna be pretty much automatic. But maybe next year, the 24-team playoff could help the debate a little bit with more teams included in the field.
